question.worked_solution:
First, note that $x=\frac{2}{3}$ is an excluded solution since division by $0$ is undefined.  

To solve the equation, we first multiply both sides by the denominator $(3x-2)$ to get rid of the fraction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8}{3x-2} & =2 \\ \frac{8(3x-2)}{(3x-2)} & =2(3x-2) \\ \frac{8\cancel{(3x-2)}}{\cancel{(3x-2)}} & =2(3x-2) \\ 8 & =6x-4\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the addition and multiplication principles, as usual:

$$
\begin{aligned}8 & =6x-4 \\ 8+4 & =6x-4+4 \\ 12 & =6x \\ \frac{12}{6} & =\frac{6x}{6} \\ 2 & =x\end{aligned}
$$

Since  $x=2$ is different from $x=\frac{2}{3}$, we can accept it as a solution. Thus, the solution is $x=2.$
